resolutions.finding: Lede: 'one of the cheapest configurations tried' is false (9 of 18 cost less).

That is true: of the five configurations at or above 97%, the pick is $0.302 per 1k and the next is brisk-s.high.r1 at $0.633 (c3 table). price_tradeoff gives cost_per_month.brisk-s.low.r1 = $1,208.00.

It states the pick's no-retry p95 ({measure.latency_ms.brisk-s.low.r0.p95} = 465 ms), so the 48 ms the retry costs is visible. items.name: First screen
items.reason: The headline, the four decision slots and c1 give the action: re-test brisk-s.low.r1 and ship it if it holds, and decide the fallback now. They give the reason: it is the only one of 18 configurations inside both gates, at 97.1% against 97% and 513 ms against 600 ms. They give the main risk: a 0.1-point clearance on a point estimate, with no configuration passing if it fails. why_not explains every rival family in one sentence each. The 'holds' condition is underspecified (item 6), but the first screen still says what to do and what is at risk.

items.name: Coherent story
items.reason: c1 (the only configuration inside both gates, lifted over by the retry) leads to c2 (the retry costs only tail latency, and high reasoning is what breaks the budget). c3 follows (the only wider clearance needs a relaxed latency budget, at {cost_per_month.brisk-s.high.r1}), then c4 (where the pick is weakest). Watch, the caveats, Explore and Next all follow from the thin margin. Nothing contradicts the headline, and the round-1 contradictions (lede cheapness, the reasoning-latency claim) are gone.

items.name: Honest emphasis
items.reason: The weak axes appear prominently: the 0.1-point margin is in the headline, Watch and c1. Multi-hop at 95.6% and ambiguous-entity at 96.4% are in Watch, c4 and the case_mix caveat. The 87 ms latency headroom is called one harness measurement. The confidence form is low. The flag names the selection optimism, and the lede's cost claim is now the narrow true one. One overstatement remains, and it is small: omitted says date math is 'above the gate' for the pick, but task.datemath.brisk-s.low.r1.pass_rate.mean is 97%, exactly the gate.

items.name: Sound elision
items.reason: None of the eight omitted items would change the call. price_tradeoff confirms one priced option ('there is no trade to price'). calls_per_task does not reorder the pass-rate clearers on a per-query basis (0.465 < 0.934 < 2.49 < 4.86 < 5.05). Extra calls and outcome hold no figures in this snapshot. The routed mix is a modeled figure, which the tool refuses to price. Explore's latency rung stops at 870 ms and leaves out the Atlas-M options admitted from 1500 ms, but those cost $1.655 to $3.477 per 1k, so leaving them out changes nothing.

items.name: Confounds handled
items.reason: Every live confound has a caveat with a material_if and a Next step: no interval (pick_clears_gate_on_point_estimate, Next 2), selection of the one inside (selection_of_the_one_inside, Next 2), eval case mix against traffic (case_mix_vs_traffic, Next 5), harness against production latency (latency_from_harness, Next 3), cost basis (Method, checked as order-preserving), and the clarification-required scoring convention (c4, Method 'Pass'). The snapshot itself lists no caveats (caveats_list is empty).

items.name: Actionable next steps
items.reason: Next 1 (declare the fallback before the result), Next 3 (p95 under load), Next 4 (read failures, then a planning directive) and Next 5 (declare the production mix) each name an action and what it settles. Next 2 does not: 'several times the current set, reporting intervals' cannot settle 'whether it really clears both gates' at a 0.1-point margin. At a true 97.1%, binomial SE is 0.28 points at 3,600 cases and 0.22 at 6,000, so a fresh point estimate lands below 97% about 32 to 36% of the time even if the pick is genuinely above. A one-sided 95% lower bound at or above 97% would need about 76,000 cases. The report never says what result counts as 'holds' (point estimate at or above the gate, or interval lower end), and the recommendation hinges on that word.

items.name: Evidence fits claims
items.reason: c1's lattice shows every configuration's gate status and the retry lift in all nine model-reasoning pairs, and the Brisk-S gate_scatter shows the corner. If the values flipped, the claim would change. c2's range_bars carry exactly what the claim says: p50 is fixed at 209 ms while p95 moves from 465 to 513 ms, and the high-reasoning rows sit above 600 ms. c3's table now carries all three axes. Two smaller misfits remain. c4's bars include brisk-s.high.r1, which no sentence uses: it lifts multi-hop to 97.3% and bears on Next 4's 'without paying for more reasoning'. And c4's examples caption is factually wrong (see findings). c3's 15-row Arm/Measure/Value layout makes the reader assemble each configuration's profile from three separate runs of rows.

findings.finding: The recommendation, Next slot and Next 2 all say 'ship it if it holds' without defining 'holds', and Next 2's re-test cannot settle the question as sized. At a true 97.1%, a re-run of 3,600 to 6,000 fresh cases has a binomial SE of 0.28 to 0.22 points. Its point estimate falls below 97% about a third of the time even when the pick is truly above, and its interval will straddle the gate almost surely: a one-sided 95% lower bound at or above 97% needs about 76,000 cases. As with the fallback in Next 1, the owner should declare before the re-test what result ships: a point estimate at or above the gate, a lower bound at or above it, or a tolerance band. Next 2's 'settles' should then say what that size can and cannot show.

The examples caption says 'The snapshot froze one failure per query type for the pick, three in all.' There are four query types. examples_list holds pick failures for multi-hop, date math and ambiguous entity only, and the fourth frozen failure (TQ-0051, single lookup) belongs to nano-xs.low.r1. Say 'one failure in each of three query types; none for single lookup'.

The bars show brisk-s.high.r1 next to the pick, but no sentence uses it. The sibling lifts multi-hop from 95.6% to 97.3% and ambiguous entity from 96.4% to 97.6%. That is the evidence that more reasoning closes the pick's weak types, and it is what Next 4 means by 'without paying for more reasoning'. State it in c4, or drop the sibling series.

Omitted, 'The date-math failure card's detail', says 'date math is above the gate for the pick'. task.datemath.brisk-s.low.r1.pass_rate.mean is 97%, exactly the gate. Say 'at the gate'. The reason for omitting still stands, because the gate reads the overall rate.

The lattice caption 'The cost label is the renderer's; Method gives the basis' talks to the reader about tooling, and the omitted scatter entry does the same ('point labels print internal ids'). The page also labels one figure two ways: '$0.302 per 1,000 replies' in the lattice and 'Cost per 1k calls' in the c3 table. Use one reader-facing label for cost on both blocks (for example, 'cost per thousand, as the snapshot measures it; Method gives the basis') and give the omission a reader-facing reason (the lattice already names every configuration).

The table renders long, as 15 Arm/Measure/Value rows, so seeing that brisk-s.high.r1 is 98% at $0.633 and 870 ms means finding three rows in three runs. One row per configuration, with pass rate, cost and p95 as columns, would show the claim (wider clearance only past the latency budget, and its price) at a glance. If the table block cannot pivot, consider whether the c1 lattice already carries this and c3 can cite it.

invariant_concerns: Invariant 1: counts written as words sit outside figure keys. 'three in all' (c4 examples caption, and factually wrong), 'one frozen failure' (Next 4 settles) and 'one harness measurement' (Watch). The digit check would not catch them. Only the first is a problem in substance.

Invariant 5: the caveat ids (for example 'pick_clears_gate_on_point_estimate', 'case_mix_vs_traffic') are snake_case internal ids. If the renderer prints caveat ids above the appendix, they break invariant 5. If it prints only material_if, no concern.
Not covered by an invariant: one cost figure carries two unit labels on the page ('per 1,000 replies' in the lattice, 'Cost per 1k calls' in the c3 table). Method discloses it.
